title: NOAA: a coral colony is many polyps that secrete a limestone skeleton
summary: NOAA says corals are made of hundreds to thousands of polyps, and that each polyp secretes a hard outer skeleton of limestone.
body: NOAA says corals are made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny coral creatures called polyps. It says each soft-bodied polyp, most no thicker than a nickel, secretes a hard outer skeleton of limestone, which is calcium carbonate. That skeleton is what the page calls the limestone foundation for coral reefs. The animal and the rock it secretes are both in that description.
